summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a complex medical history including chronic diastolic heart failure, type II diabetes, chronic kidney disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and chronic pain following knee replacement was readmitted due to persistent right-sided chest pain after multiple falls. She presented with worsening fatigue and dark urine. Evaluation revealed acute kidney injury and a urinary tract infection, likely exacerbated by chronic narcotic use and dehydration. Chest imaging showed no rib fractures but confirmed bibasilar atelectasis. She was treated with antibiotics and supportive care, with improvement in renal function and resolution of infection. Given her recurrent falls and difficulty managing pain and mobility at home, she agreed to a post-discharge rehabilitation stay focused on physical therapy, pain management, and fall prevention. She was discharged stable with follow-up plans and a coordinated transition to rehab.
